cmp.label: Comparison
cmp.title:
Why not Telegram
or Signal?
cmp.desc: All popular messengers store your data on their servers. Mess&Anger is the only one where data lives exclusively on your device.
feat.label: Features
feat.title:
Everything you need.
Nothing you don't.
feat.desc: Every feature ships with privacy and security baked in. No toggle to turn off — because you shouldn't have to choose between usability and anonymity.
feat.p1: WebRTC creates an encrypted tunnel directly between you and your contact. No server ever sees your messages — there's nothing in between.
feat.p2: Signal-style E2EE: X25519/Ed25519 key agreement, a fresh key per message and AES-256-GCM at rest. The protocol spec is open for review.
feat.p3: Identity is your cryptographic fingerprint (a BIP-39 seed you back up). Add contacts via QR code, username, or nova:// link.
sec.label: Security architecture
sec.title:
Defense
in depth
sec.desc: From RFC 5869 HKDF to per-message ratchet keys. Each layer is independent — if one is compromised, the rest hold. Full protocol spec in the repository.
sec.l2: Sealed sender + safety numbers for key verification
sec.l3: Unique key per message. On all chats, not just secret.
sec.l6: AES-256-GCM + PBKDF2 for storage at rest. 600k iterations.
stars.label: Stars Economy
stars.title:
Earn by
supporting the network
stars.desc: Stars is a local reward system. Not crypto, not blockchain. Just motivation for those who keep the network alive.
ac.label: Anti-censorship
ac.title:
Hard
to block
ac.desc: Several transports with automatic fallback. Not magic: a censor who blocks every endpoint can still cut access — which is why you can run and register your own relay.
ac.l1d: Standard P2P. Direct encrypted tunnel with no intermediaries.
ac.l3d: Fake TLS headers, XOR, random padding, timing jitter.
ac.l4d: Run your own signaling/relay gateway so blocking one domain does not break the network.
ac.l5d: WebRTC → WS tunnel → obfuscated transport. Automatic.

faq.label: FAQ
faq.title:
Frequently
asked questions
faq.q1: What if I lose my phone?
faq.a1: If you created an encrypted backup (.nova-backup file) or saved your 24-word recovery phrase — restore your account on a new device. Without one of them, data is lost forever.
faq.a2: Hard, not impossible. Traffic can run over WebRTC, a WebSocket tunnel or obfuscated transports, and you can add your own relay — but a sufficiently resourced censor can still block the app’s endpoints.
faq.a3: Only you and the recipient. Messages are encrypted on your device and decrypted only on the recipient's device.
faq.a4: Not yet. Nova uses the classical Signal stack (X3DH + Double Ratchet). A hybrid post-quantum handshake is on the roadmap; Signal made the same transition with PQXDH.
faq.q5: How do I add a contact?
faq.a5: Scan a QR code, find by username, or get a nova:// link. There is no central address book.
faq.a6: No. Stars is a local activity reward system. No blockchain, no market value.
